newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGE sees 1997 operating profit improving.
newsitem.headline: CGE sees 1997 operating profit improving.

text.p: French water company Cie Generale des Eaux (CGE) expects 1996 operating profit to double, exceeding 1994's 3.7 billion francs and that the improvement should continue in 1997, chairman Jean-Marie Messier said.

Operating profit for 1996 "will more than double and should be higher than the 3.7 billion reached in 1994, despite the departure of some activities from the consolidated structure. This improvement should continue in 1997," Messier told the Investir weekly, due to appear on Saturday.
He also reiterated a forecast for 1996 net profit of 1.8 billion francs.
Messier said that "taking into account recent developments," his forecast of a net profit for 1997 of four billion francs was a "very conservative" estimate.
Funds raised from a recent conversion of a convertible bonds, worth around five billion francs, would be used to repay debt, he said.
By the end of the year, the net debt-to-equity ratio will be halved, or even better than that, compared to a ratio of 1.7 two years ago, he said.

"I believe that for a business like ours, largely predictable and supported in a number of its activities by long-term contracts, an optimal balance sheet structure should have a ratio close to 0.75. We are almost there," he said.
"Most of the rebalancing of the balance sheet of Generale des Eaux will be done by the end of 1997. That is good news," he said.
